title: Split Schubert boundary Picard basis over arbitrary fields
statement: Let $F$ be any field [def-weil-field] and $H$ a reductive $F$-group with split maximal torus $T$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. A reductive group means a smooth affine group of finite type, geometrically connected, whose extension to an algebraic closure has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology, def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]. A split maximal torus means a maximal torus isomorphic over the ground field to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. A Borel subgroup is a smooth connected closed subgroup maximal among the connected solvable subgroups, where solvable means having a finite normal series with commutative successive quotients [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]. Let $B\supseteq T$ be a Borel subgroup which is split solvable, meaning it admits a finite normal series with successive quotients $\mathbf G_a$ or $\mathbf G_m$ [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors]. Let $Q=H/B$ denote the represented fppf sheaf quotient, the sheafification of $A\mapsto H(A)/B(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented covers. For every scheme $Y$, $\operatorname{Pic}(Y)$ is the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, with tensor product as addition; invertible means locally free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. Pullback means tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. There are $d,s\geq0$, an open immersion $j:\mathbf A^d_F\hookrightarrow Q$ with dense image [def-weil-open-immersion, def-sbc-affine-space], and geometrically integral effective Cartier divisors $D_1,\ldots,D_s$ on $Q$ whose supports are the distinct codimension-one irreducible components of $Q\setminus j(\mathbf A^d_F)$. An effective Cartier divisor means a closed subscheme whose ideal is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]; geometrically integral means integral and nonempty after every field extension. Write $\mathcal O_Q(D_i)=\mathcal I_{D_i}^{\vee}$. The homomorphism $$\mathbf Z^s\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Pic}(Q),\qquad(m_i)\longmapsto\left[\bigotimes_i\mathcal O_Q(D_i)^{\otimes m_i}\right]$$ is an isomorphism, where negative tensor powers mean powers of the dual. For every extension $L/F$ [def-pc-field-extension], the scalar extended open cell and divisors have the same properties on $Q_L=H_L/B_L$, the classes of $\mathcal O_{Q_L}(D_{i,L})$ give the same basis, and pullback $p_Q^*$ sends $[\mathcal O_Q(D_i)]$ to $[\mathcal O_{Q_L}(D_{i,L})]$. The cases $H=T$ and $H=1$ have $s=d=0$ and $Q=\operatorname{Spec}F$.

source.place: Brion, On Linearization of Line Bundles, Lemma 2.3 proof, printed p.118, the Pic(G/B) and root-datum paragraph, citing Iversen 1976 Proposition 5.2 and Theorem 5.3. The explicit split Schubert-boundary basis and its scalar-extension form are the geometric input unpacked here; also Milne Lemma 18.21, printed p.392, the split affine-cell argument. The statement concerns split groups over arbitrary fields, not only algebraically closed fields.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-bruhat-affine-stratification]. Put $U=C_{a_0}\simeq\mathbf A_F^d$. This is open dense, and $Q$ is smooth projective geometrically integral. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] it is regular and locally Noetherian; by [lem-pc-projective-proper] it is proper, hence finite type and separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Local Noetherianity and the quasi-compactness in [def-pc-projective-morphism] give Noetherianity. The same conclusions hold over every extension field. Thus the regular Noetherian separated divisor dictionary [lem-sfb-regular-space-divisor-line-dictionary] applies.

In the finite stratification, choose the maximal distinct closures of strata other than $C_{a_0}$. Since the complement is closed and consists of all the other cells, these are exactly the irreducible components of $Q\setminus U$: the complement is the union of those finitely many closures, and an irreducible subset of a finite union of closed subsets is contained in one of them. Give them the reduced closed structures $D_i$. Each is the scheme-theoretic image of its affine-space stratum by [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image]. Because stratum immersions are quasi-compact in this Noetherian scheme, [lem-sfb-scheme-image-flat-base-change] applies to every field extension: on an affine chart $R$, the extension is $R\to R\otimes_F L$, a free $R$-module by an $F$-basis of $L$, and hence flat. It identifies $(D_i)_L$ with the reduced closure of the corresponding $\mathbf A_L^{n_i}$. This closure is nonempty reduced irreducible, so $D_i$ is geometrically integral. Apply this closure comparison also to each nonmaximal stratum. Inclusions among all the closures are preserved and reflected by the surjective projection $Q_L\to Q$: for subsets $A,B$, surjectivity gives $q^{-1}A\subseteq q^{-1}B$ if and only if $A\subseteq B$. Thus precisely the same maximal closures, with no new inclusions or equalities, are the boundary components over $L$.

source.place: Theorem 21.80 and Bruhat cell closures; Stacks Tags 056B (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-reduced) and 081I (lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image).

proof.text: Since $U$ is dense affine in the separated locally Noetherian $Q$ (step 1), [lem-sfb-affine-open-boundary-codimension-one] gives $\dim\mathcal O_{Q,\xi_i}=1$ at the generic point $\xi_i$ of each $D_i$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $\mathcal I_i$ be the ideal of $D_i$ and $y\in Q$. If $y\notin D_i$, then $(\mathcal I_i)_y=\mathcal O_{Q,y}$ is generated by $1$. If $y\in D_i$, choose an affine open $y\in V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The nonempty open $D_i\cap V$ of the irreducible $D_i$ contains $\xi_i$, so it is $V(\mathfrak q)$ for the prime $\mathfrak q$ of $\xi_i$, and [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] (1) gives $\mathcal I_i|_V=\widetilde{\mathfrak q}$. Let $\mathfrak p\supseteq\mathfrak q$ be the prime of $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] (c), $A=\mathcal O_{Q,y}=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathcal O_{Q,\xi_i}=R_{\mathfrak q}$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] $(\mathcal I_i)_y=\mathfrak qA$, a prime of $A$ whose smaller primes correspond to the primes of $R_{\mathfrak q}$. As $\dim R_{\mathfrak q}=1$, it is nonzero of height one. The local ring $A$ is regular (step 1), hence a Noetherian unique factorization domain by [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] with $r=0$, and [lem-trf-ufd-height-one], (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii), gives $\mathfrak qA=(f_i)$ with $f_i\ne0$, a nonzerodivisor of the domain $A$. The scheme form of [lem-sfb-stalk-nonzerodivisor-cartier-spreading] now shows that $\mathcal I_i$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. The same argument over $L$, for the components $D_{i,L}$ of step 2 in the regular $Q_L$, shows that the actual base changes $D_{i,L}$ are geometrically integral effective Cartier divisors with exactly the required supports.

source.place: Tags 0AGA (lemma-weil-divisor-is-cartier-UFD) and 0AFT (algebra.tex, lemma-characterize-UFD-height-1), with Milne iAG2017 Lemma 18.21, p.392; Stacks 0EGJ (lemma-complement-open-affine-effective-cartier-divisor-bis) for the codimension-one boundary.

proof.text: Every invertible module $M$ on $Q$ is trivial on $U$ by [lem-sfb-affine-space-invertible-trivial]. Regard a chosen generator on $U$ as a rational section $s$ of $M$. The dictionary [lem-sfb-regular-space-divisor-line-dictionary] gives $M\simeq\mathcal O_Q(\operatorname{div}(s))$. Since $s$ generates on $U$, its divisor has no codimension-one support there; the only remaining prime divisors are the $D_i$. Thus $\operatorname{div}(s)=\sum_i m_iD_i$. Locally, if $D_i$ has equation $f_i$, this divisor has equation $\prod_i f_i^{m_i}$, and its invertible module is $\prod_i f_i^{-m_i}\mathcal O_Q$. Tensoring the local generators gives $\mathcal O_Q(\sum_i m_iD_i)\simeq\bigotimes_i\mathcal O_Q(D_i)^{\otimes m_i}$. By [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] these are exactly the dual ideals in the statement. This proves surjectivity.

source.place: Lemma 18.21 proof, p.392: affine-cell trivialization and boundary divisors.

proof.text: Suppose $\bigotimes_i\mathcal O_Q(D_i)^{\otimes m_i}$ is trivial. Under this trivialization its canonical rational section becomes a rational function $f$ with divisor $\sum_i m_iD_i$. On $U$ the divisor is zero, so the dictionary makes $f|_U$ an everywhere generating section of $\mathcal O_U$, a polynomial unit. Such a unit is a nonzero constant: if polynomials $a,b$ over a field satisfy $ab=1$, their highest homogeneous parts have nonzero product, so $\deg(ab)=\deg a+\deg b$ forces both degrees to be zero (including $d=0$). Consequently $f$ equals a nonzero constant in the function field, since $U$ is dense. Its divisor is zero. The distinct prime divisors $D_i$ are formal generators of the Weil-divisor group, so all $m_i=0$. This proves injectivity.

source.place: Lemma 18.21 proof, p.392; agent-supplied explicit independence argument from polynomial units.

proof.text: For $L/F$, steps 1–3 give the scalar-extended open and divisors with the same properties, so steps 4–5 over $L$ prove that their classes are a basis. The projection $p_Q$ is flat, being a field-extension base change. Flat pullback in [lem-sfb-regular-space-divisor-line-dictionary] gives $p_Q^*\mathcal O_Q(D_i)\simeq\mathcal O_{Q_L}(D_{i,L})$; locally it sends $f_i^{-1}$ to the inverse of the pulled-back equation, hence is the identification for the actual Cartier base change. If $H=T$ (including $H=1$), the Bruhat statement gives $Q=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $U=\mathbf A_F^0$; there are no boundary components and $s=d=0$, as required.

source.place: Brion Lemma 2.3, p.118, field-extension compatibility; Milne Theorem 21.80 and Lemma 18.21; flat pullback of local Cartier equations.
